summary: S-PF-01 delivered the E-PRODUCT-FOUNDATION-001 W0 telemetry seam: every scaffolded product now ships a track(event,props) seam with a pluggable PostHog/no-op sink, the six canonical lifecycle events, fail-closed activation-definition derivation, and supply-chain telemetry-chain evaluation. The lastmile analytics module was re-pointed to enrich rather than reinstall. The scaffold-coverage enforcer gained telemetry/security checks hardened across three OpenAI security-review rounds and three OpenAI backend-review rounds (both ultimately PASS). The release RL-20260611-045 was prepared by Codex with approval as the only open gate; the operator-instructed Claude session 2026-06-12 ground-truthed the work (validators green, suites green, cross-family spot-review PASS), recorded approval AP-20260612-029, and deployed to internal-canary. The same branch also carried S-PF-02 through S-PF-08 as epic work items, taking the epic to ~98%.

outcomes_shipped.outcome: Scaffold telemetry seam: events.ts/sink.ts/track.ts/chain.ts templates with exact lifecycle event vocabulary, one sink resolver, fail-open track boundary, and correlation/broken-chain evaluation.
evidence: commit a404f02 feat(S-PF-01): add scaffold telemetry seam

outcomes_shipped.outcome: Scaffold-coverage enforcer hardened against raw-emit bypasses (analytics.track, sendBeacon, raw fetch outside sink.ts), comment-spoofing, commented-out vocabulary, missing named exports, and invalid activation metadata — via security/backend review fix-cycles.
Lastmile analytics module enriches the scaffold seam instead of reinstalling; activation revisions are fail-closed validated and emit activation_definition_change with changedFields.
Release RL-20260611-045 approved (AP-20260612-029, operator-instructed) and deployed to internal-canary; sprint closed.
evidence: release.js check --id RL-20260611-045 ready=true after approve
release.js deploy: sprint S-PF-01 status releasing -> closed
routing coverage ok:true (qa x2, redteam x1)

outcomes_shipped.outcome: Named wave-style sprint ids (S-PF-01) accepted across ledger/routing/fs/guards/schemas, with regression proof.

plan_quality_actual.predicted_status: W0 telemetry seam per Product Lead build_spec, telemetry-first per DoP ruling
evidence_gaps_actual: build_spec cited message_brief-E-PRODUCT-FOUNDATION-001-w0 before it existed; the artifact had to be minted first because validate-artifact.js rejects dangling references.
Several sprint validators only accepted dated SP-YYYYMMDD-NNN ids and had to be extended for named wave ids.
Review lanes ran OpenAI-on-OpenAI (GPT executor + GPT reviewers, recorded honestly as single_vendor_session); cross-family assurance arrived later via the Claude audit 2026-06-12.
plan_quality_actual.notes: The plan held; the seam shipped exactly telemetry-first. The fix-cycles were productive — each review round closed real bypass classes in the enforcer rather than cosmetic findings.

scope_variant_actual.drift_notes: Release approval was deliberately left to the operator; the 2026-06-12 session recorded it from an explicit operator instruction (mint a new WarpOS version) rather than inferring it from older chat.

surprises.surprise: The duplicate raw-sink detector needed three review rounds to cover analytics.track, sendBeacon, and raw fetch variants — each round found a new same-class bypass.
surprises.impact: Two extra security re-review dispatches before the redteam routing trace could be recorded.

surprises.surprise: release.js check mutates the release YAML updated_at as a read side effect, dirtying the working tree.
surprises.impact: Codex had to restore the committed timestamp twice during wrap.

friction_points.friction: Same-family review (GPT reviewing GPT-built work) was the only available lane during the Codex session; honest single_vendor_session labels preserved auditability but cross-family verification had to be retrofitted.
evidence: Claude audit 2026-06-12 provided the cross-family pass

friction_points.friction: Named sprint ids were rejected by multiple validators (ledger, routing, fs, tracker guards, schemas), requiring a mid-sprint validator extension.

action_items.action: Fix release.js check so a read-only gate check does not rewrite updated_at in the release YAML.
When the executing family equals the reviewing family, schedule a cross-family audit before ship — encode as a routing-evidence expectation rather than ad-hoc.

learning_candidates.learning: Enforcer hardening converges fastest when each review round must produce a planted fixture for the bypass it found — the S-PF-01 scanner grew from 9 to 25 fixture cases across three rounds and each new case was a real bypass class.
single_vendor_session routing labels make same-family review debt visible and dischargeable later; the Claude audit could target exactly the lanes that lacked cross-family eyes.
